question: Simplify \(x(2x-3)-2x(x-1)\), and find its value when \(x=5\).

provenance.contribution: Existing attributed explanation retained; project contribution is review and annotations.
provenance.reviewStatus: Current explanation retained and independently AI-reviewed; not teacher reviewed

solutionMethods.explanation:
Both terms have a factor \(x\), so factor it out to simplify one bracket:
\[
x(2x-3)-2x(x-1)=x\bigl[(2x-3)-2(x-1)\bigr].
\]
The bracket equals \(2x-3-2x+2=-1\). Thus the expression is \(-x\), and when \(x=5\), its value is \(-5\).
solutionMethods.label: Factor out x

reference.question: Simplify \(x(2x-3)-2x(x-1)\), and find its value when \(x=5\).
reference.solution:
Method 1: Expand and combine

\(x(2x-3)-2x(x-1)=2x^2-3x-2x^2+2x=-x\). When \(x=5\), the value is \(-5\).

Method 2: Factor out x

Both terms have a factor \(x\), so factor it out to simplify one bracket:
\[
x(2x-3)-2x(x-1)=x\bigl[(2x-3)-2(x-1)\bigr].
\]
The bracket equals \(2x-3-2x+2=-1\). Thus the expression is \(-x\), and when \(x=5\), its value is \(-5\).

nodes.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.* Examples: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known.
